Mamurra, a Roman commander born in Formiae
la:other:Mamurra.html:
Māmurra, ae, m.,
a Roman knight of Formiæ, praefectus fabrūm in Gaul under Cæsar, who was the first in Rome to cover the walls of his house on the Mons Cœlius with marble, and had none but marble columns in his house, ; cf. ; ; ; : Mamurrarum urbs,i. e. Formiæ,.

la:noun:mamma.html:
mamma, ae, f., = μάμμα,
a breast, pap, esp. of females, rarely of males; also, a teat, dug of animals.
Lit.: puero isti date mammam,give him the breast, suckle him,; : puer in gremio matris sedens, mammam appetens,: ubera mammarum,.—Of a man: mammas homo solus e maribus habet,; ; —Of animals, : mammam sugere,: mammas praebere,: mamma sterilescit,dries up, —
Transf.
A protuberance on the bark of a tree, .—
In the language of children, mother, mamma: cum cibum ac potionem buas ac papas vocent, matrem mammam, patrem tatam, Varr. ap. ; . —In inscrr., for mother, ; ; for grandmother, Inscr. Mur. 1134, 3; for nurse, Inscr. Visc. Mus. Pio-Clem. t. 2, p. 82.
